SHARED.YES: Button label answering the exit confirmation dialog ("Leave Osm Go!?"); also the yes option on the survey-date card. Short.
SHARED.NO: Button label (cancel side) of the exit confirmation dialog "Leave Osm Go!?". Short answer, not the word for a count of zero.
SHARED.CANCEL: Button label, imperative. Dismisses a dialog, editor or marker placement without applying anything. Reused in many places and as a tooltip/aria-label. Short.
SHARED.CONFIRM: Button label, imperative. Confirms the action in a generic confirmation dialog (e.g. deleting an object, leaving the editor, uploading). Short.
SHARED.ADD: Button label / aria-label, imperative. Adds the typed value as a new entry in a multi-value field (e.g. a list of values for a tag) or adds a new tag. Short.
SHARED.OK: Action button of the "Load data?" toast on the map (MAIN.LOAD_BBOX); it starts the download. Very short.
SHARED.CLOSE: Button label, imperative, also aria-label of X buttons and the action on toast messages (snackbars). Dismisses a page, dialog or message without changing data. Short.
SHARED.LOADING: Status text on the startup screen while the app loads its local data. Progressive state, no action. Short.
SHARED.CREATE: Button label, imperative, in the editor footer when adding a NEW OpenStreetMap object: validates and creates it locally (not yet uploaded). Short.
SHARED.EDIT: Button label, imperative, in the selected-object sheet: opens the editor for the selected map object. Short.
SHARED.SEARCH: Placeholder of the search field filtering the list of categories (presets) in the tag management screens. Short.
SHARED.DELETE: Imperative verb. Tooltip and aria-label of the trash icon button in the editor that deletes the OpenStreetMap object, and of icon buttons removing an opening-hours entry. Short.
SHARED.ERROR: Toast message after a failed save or action in the object sheet or editor. Reassures that the user's edits were kept (still in the form / stored locally) and can be retried. Full sentence.
SHARED.NO_RESULTS: Empty-state message shown when a search or list (base maps, active categories) has no matching item. Short.
SHARED.RETRY: Button label, imperative, in the base map list after loading failed: runs the request again. Short.
SHARED.CLEAR_FIELD: aria-label (screen reader) of the small button that empties a form field. {{field}} is the field's label or tag key, shown in the quotes; keep the quotes/placeholder. Typographic quotes are intentional.

A11Y.ADD_BOOKMARK: aria-label / tooltip of a star icon button that bookmarks a category (preset) as favorite so it appears in the favorites list. Toggles with REMOVE_BOOKMARK. Imperative.
A11Y.CATEGORY_SOURCE: aria-label (screen reader only, not visible) of the toggle group that switches the category list between recently used, favorites and all categories.
A11Y.CENTER_FEATURE: aria-label (screen reader only) of an icon button on each item of the upload screen: pans the map to this changed object. Imperative.
A11Y.CHANGE_SUMMARY: aria-label (screen reader only) of the summary block on the upload screen with counts of created, modified and deleted objects. Noun phrase.
A11Y.CODE: Tooltip and aria-label of an icon button that toggles display of raw OpenStreetMap tag codes (keys and values like amenity=cafe) next to the human labels. Do not translate the toggled codes.
A11Y.COPY_FIELDS: Button label and aria-label in the editor of an existing object: stores its current field values so they can be pasted into a new object later. Imperative; fits a medium button.
A11Y.HIDE_TAG: aria-label (screen reader only) of an icon button that hides a category (tag preset) from the category lists. "Tag" here means an OSM category preset. Imperative.
A11Y.MAIN_NAVIGATION: aria-label (screen reader only) of the main menu navigation landmark. Noun phrase.
A11Y.OBJECT_FIELDS: aria-label (screen reader only) of the form region holding the editable fields of the OpenStreetMap object. Noun phrase.
A11Y.OPEN_LINK: aria-label (screen reader only) of an icon button next to a URL field; opens the link in the browser. Imperative.
A11Y.OSM_ACCOUNT: aria-label (screen reader only) of the account card in the menu showing the logged-in OpenStreetMap user. Keep "OpenStreetMap" untranslated.
A11Y.PASTE_FIELDS: Button label and aria-label in the editor of a new object: fills the form with the fields remembered from the last object. {{category}} is the name of the object's category (e.g. Restaurant). Imperative; keep the dot separator.
A11Y.REMOVE_BOOKMARK: aria-label / tooltip of a filled star icon button that removes a category from favorites. Opposite of ADD_BOOKMARK. Imperative.
A11Y.REMOVE_TAG: aria-label (screen reader only) of a trash icon button deleting one raw OpenStreetMap tag (key=value) from the object in the editor. Imperative.
A11Y.SELECTED: aria-label of a check icon marking the category currently used by the object in the category list. Screen reader only; adjective, singular.
A11Y.SHOW_TAG: aria-label (screen reader only) of an eye icon button in the hidden categories list: makes a hidden category visible again. Imperative.
A11Y.USE_OSM_DEV_SERVER: aria-label (screen reader only) of the toggle in Settings > Developer mode that sends uploads to the OpenStreetMap test (development) server instead of production. Imperative.

MAIN.EXIT_CONFIRM_HEADER: Title of the confirmation dialog shown when the user presses back or leaves the app on the map. Short question; buttons are Yes / No.
MAIN.EXIT_CONFIRM_MESSAGE: Body of the exit confirmation dialog, answered with Yes/No buttons. Keep "Osm Go!" (app name) untranslated, including the exclamation mark.
MAIN.START_SNACK_ITEMS_IN_MEMORY: Toast shown at startup, e.g. "123 items in memory". {{count}} is the number of OpenStreetMap objects already downloaded on the device (1 or more).
MAIN.WHAT_ITEM: Title of the dialog shown when several map objects overlap at the tapped point. Very short question.
MAIN.SELECT_ITEM_AT_LOCATION: Instruction under the title in the dialog listing overlapping objects; the user taps one row to select it. "Object" = OpenStreetMap feature (point of interest, building, etc.).
MAIN.LOAD_BBOX: Toast shown on the map suggesting to download OpenStreetMap data for the visible area (bbox = bounding box). Its action button (SHARED.OK) triggers the download. Short question.

STARTUP.TITLE: Heading of the full-screen error shown when the app fails to start (local data or a required resource cannot be loaded). Followed by one of the explanatory messages below.
STARTUP.REQUIRED_RESOURCE_FAILED: Error message under the startup error heading when a file the app needs (e.g. preset or translation data) failed to load. "Resource" = app file, not a map resource. Tells the user to retry.
STARTUP.CORRUPTED_STORAGE: Error message on the startup error screen when the saved data on the device (downloaded OSM objects and pending, not yet uploaded edits) is damaged. Refers to the two buttons Try again and Reset local map data. Keep their names consistent.
STARTUP.RETRY: Button label, imperative, on the startup error screen: reloads the app. Short.
STARTUP.RESET_LOCAL_DATA: Destructive button label, imperative, on the startup error screen: erases downloaded map data and pending edits stored on the device (a backup is attempted first). Must match wording in CORRUPTED_STORAGE.
STARTUP.QUARANTINE_NOTICE: Toast shown after startup when damaged saved objects were set aside. {{count}} is the number of such objects (number, can be 1). Refers to the Upload screen, where they can be exported to a file. Mind plural.
STARTUP.RESET_FAILED: Toast shown when the reset button could not make a backup of the local data first, so nothing was erased. Reassuring tone.

MAP_INITIALIZATION.TITLE: Heading of an error banner shown over the map when the map cannot start. Followed by one of the messages below and a Try again button.
MAP_INITIALIZATION.STYLE_FAILED: Error message in the map error banner: the map style (map tiles design, fetched from the network) could not be loaded. Tells the user to retry.
MAP_INITIALIZATION.WEBGL_REQUIRED: Error message in the map error banner: the device or browser lacks WebGL 2 (graphics technology). Keep "WebGL 2" as is.
MAP_INITIALIZATION.CREATION_FAILED: Error message in the map error banner: generic failure creating the map. Suggests retrying, then restarting the app.
MAP_INITIALIZATION.RETRY: Button label, imperative, in the map error banner: tries to start the map again. Short.

OVERLAY.LABEL: aria-label (screen reader only) of the dialog that holds secondary screens (settings, upload, etc.) laid over the map. Written as "OsmGo" here, unlike the app name "Osm Go!": keep the product name as is. Noun phrase.

SELECTION.SELECTED_OBJECT: aria-label (screen reader only) of the bottom sheet describing the currently selected map object. Noun phrase.
SELECTION.RESIZE_PANEL: aria-label (screen reader only) of the drag handle that lets users resize the bottom sheet by sliding it. Imperative.

STACK.LABEL: aria-label (screen reader only) of the navigation bar for browsing between several objects located at the same point. Noun phrase.
STACK.PREVIOUS: Tooltip and aria-label of a left-arrow icon button: show the previous object among those at the same spot. Short.
STACK.NEXT: Tooltip and aria-label of a right-arrow icon button: show the next object among those at the same spot. Short.
STACK.LIST: Tooltip of the "2 / 3" counter button; opens the dialog listing every object at that point. Imperative.
STACK.POSITION: aria-label (screen reader only) of the "2 / 3" counter button. {{index}} is the current position (1-based number), {{count}} the total number of objects. Mind the sentence reads as "2 of 3"; keep placeholders.

SELECTION.EXPAND_PANEL: Tooltip and aria-label of the button that makes the object bottom sheet taller (full detail). Imperative. Counterpart of REDUCE_PANEL.
SELECTION.REDUCE_PANEL: Tooltip and aria-label of the button that makes the object bottom sheet shorter again. Imperative. Counterpart of EXPAND_PANEL.
SELECTION.ADD_BOOKMARK: Tooltip and aria-label of the star icon button in the object sheet: saves this object's category as a favorite. Imperative; toggles with REMOVE_BOOKMARK.
SELECTION.REMOVE_BOOKMARK: Tooltip and aria-label of the filled star icon button in the object sheet: removes this object's category from favorites. Imperative.
SELECTION.DISCARD_TITLE: Title of the confirmation dialog when the user closes the editor with unsaved edits (also in the opening-hours interval editor). Question.
SELECTION.DISCARD_MESSAGE: Body of the unsaved-changes dialog. Buttons: Cancel and Discard. Short warning.
SELECTION.DISCARD: Destructive confirm button label, imperative: drops unsaved edits or local changes. Used in the unsaved-changes dialog and the revert dialog. Short.

METADATA.LABEL: aria-label (screen reader only) of the line below the title of the object sheet showing OpenStreetMap edit history (who/when/version). Keep "OpenStreetMap".
METADATA.CREATED: Prefix of the history line, followed by a relative time and author: e.g. "Created 3 days ago · Alice". Place so the time can follow; past participle.
METADATA.UPDATED: Prefix of the history line, followed by a relative time and author: e.g. "Updated 2 hours ago · Alice". Used when the object version is above 1. Past participle.
METADATA.PENDING: Prefix of the history line for an object created on this device and not yet uploaded to OpenStreetMap; followed by " · " and the user's name. Short status.

FIELDS.ARTIST: Short field label in the object sheet summary for the OSM tag artist_name (the artist of an artwork or statue). Do not translate the tag key.
FIELDS.MATERIAL: Short field label in the object sheet summary for the OSM tag material (what an object is made of).
FIELDS.START_DATE: Short field label in the object sheet summary for the OSM tag start_date (date the object began or was built).
FIELDS.OPTION_VALUE: Format of one item in a multi-choice list of the summary when its value is not just yes. {{label}} is the option name (e.g. Credit cards), {{value}} is the value text (such as the words for no or only). Keep the colon and placeholders.
FIELDS.VALUE_NO: Lowercase value word shown after an option label, e.g. "Cards: no"; means this option is not available (OSM value no).
FIELDS.VALUE_ONLY: Lowercase value word shown after an option label, e.g. "Dogs: only"; means exclusively this option (OSM value only).

SELECTION.REVERT_LOCAL: Button label, imperative, in the object sheet for an object with local, not yet uploaded changes; also confirm button on the upload screen. Resets it to the last downloaded OSM version.
SELECTION.REVERT_LOCAL_TITLE: Title of the confirmation dialog for discarding the user's local changes to one object (object sheet, editor, upload screen). Question.
SELECTION.REVERT_LOCAL_MESSAGE: Body of the revert dialog for an object whose edits are local. Explains that it returns to the last version fetched from OpenStreetMap.
SELECTION.REVERT_LOCAL_MESSAGE_CREATED: Body of the revert dialog for a newly created object that is not uploaded: discarding removes it entirely. Warning.
SELECTION.REVERT_LOCAL_MESSAGE_DELETED: Body of the revert dialog for an object the user marked for deletion: discarding keeps the object instead of deleting it.

BUTTONS.MENU: Tooltip and aria-label of the hamburger icon button on the map that opens the main menu. Noun.
BUTTONS.UPLOAD: Tooltip and aria-label of the icon button on the map that opens the upload screen to send local edits to OpenStreetMap. Imperative or noun; short.
BUTTONS.LOAD_DATA: Tooltip of the refresh button on the map: downloads OpenStreetMap data of the visible area. Imperative.
BUTTONS.REFRESH_DATA: Visible label and aria-label of the floating button on the map that downloads/refreshes OSM data for the visible area. Imperative, short (small pill button).
BUTTONS.LOADING_DATA: Visible label and aria-label of the same button while download is running, next to a spinner. Present participle; very short.
BUTTONS.VIEW_AREAL_MAP: Tooltip and aria-label of a map layer button: switches from the vector map to satellite/aerial photography. Key name says "AREAL" but it means aerial. Imperative.
BUTTONS.VIEW_STYLED_MAP: Tooltip and aria-label of a map layer button: switches back from aerial imagery to the standard map. Imperative.
BUTTONS.ADD_NEW: Tooltip and aria-label of the "+" floating button: starts creating a new OpenStreetMap object on the map. "Object" = point of interest. Imperative.
BUTTONS.CENTER_GPS: Tooltip and aria-label of the crosshair icon button: pans the map to the user's GPS position. Imperative.
BUTTONS.CONFIRM_ADD: Tooltip and aria-label of the check button when placing a new object on the map: validates the location, then the editor opens. Imperative.
BUTTONS.CONFIRM_MOVE: Tooltip and aria-label of buttons (map and editor) for relocating an existing object: starts or validates the move. Imperative; also on the editor's move icon button.
BUTTONS.REFRESH_ZOOM_HINT: Hint (tooltip on the disabled download button and toast) telling users to zoom the map in before data can be downloaded. Imperative.

LOCATION.DENIED: Toast shown when the user taps the locate button but location permission is refused. Tells the user to enable it in the device or browser settings.
LOCATION.UNAVAILABLE: Toast shown when the locate button is tapped but no position is available (GPS off or no signal).
LOCATION.SEARCHING: Toast shown while waiting for the first GPS position after tapping the locate button. Ongoing action.

SW.INSTALLATION_FAILED: Top toast (web app only) when an update of the app could not be installed; its action is Reload. "Version" = app version.
SW.UNRECOVERABLE: Top toast (web app only) when the app's cached files are broken and must be reloaded; action button is Reload.
SW.RELOAD: Action button label on the top toasts about app updates or sync problems; reloads the page. Imperative, very short.
SW.EXTERNAL_STATE: Top toast (web app only) when another browser tab modified the same stored data. Action button is Reload.

MAIN.LINKED_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND: Toast shown when the app was opened through a link to a specific OpenStreetMap object, which is absent from the data downloaded on the device.

MENU.CONNECTION: Menu item in the side menu, shown only when logged out; starts OpenStreetMap OAuth login. Short (one menu row). Keep 'OpenStreetMap' as is.
MENU.SETTINGS: Menu item in the side menu opening the Settings screen. Short noun, one word if possible.
MENU.ABOUT: Menu item in the side menu opening the About screen (version, data credits, GitHub). Short.
MENU.DELETE_DATA: Button at the bottom of the side menu (red, trash icon) that deletes the downloaded map data, keeping edits. Short imperative verb phrase.
MENU.DELETE_DATA_CONFIRM_HEADER: Title of the confirmation dialog opened by the 'Delete data' menu button. Short question.
MENU.DELETE_DATA_CONFIRM_MESSAGE: Body of the 'Delete data' confirmation dialog. 'Downloaded data' = cached OSM map objects; the parentheses say that unsent local edits are kept. Question.
MENU.SIGN_OUT: Button in the side menu footer, shown only when logged in, to end the OpenStreetMap session. Short imperative verb phrase; the mirror of the login item.
MENU.NEW_VERSION: Bold first line of the update banner at the top of the side menu, shown when a new app version has been downloaded. Short exclamatory phrase.
MENU.INSTALL_UPDATE: Smaller second line of the update banner in the side menu, under 'New version available!'. Tapping reloads the app to apply the update. Imperative, short.
MENU.TAG_MANAGEMENT: Menu item in the side menu opening the screen to enable or hide tag presets (types of objects offered when adding a point). 'Tag' is the OSM term; use the established OSM translation. Short.
MENU.LOGIN_ERROR: Snackbar (toast) shown when starting the OpenStreetMap login fails; shown with a Close action. Keep 'OpenStreetMap' as is. Two short sentences.

ABOUT.ABOUT: Title of the About screen header. Short, same as MENU.ABOUT.
ABOUT.DATA: Label of a list row in the About screen; the line below credits the map data source. Single noun.
ABOUT.VERSION: Label of a list row in the About screen; the app version number (e.g. 3.0.0) is displayed below it. Single noun.
ABOUT.OSM_CONTRIBUTORS: Standard OpenStreetMap data attribution line under the 'Data' row. Keep the (c) sign and 'OpenStreetMap' as is, in the usual official form of the translated attribution ('contributors' translated per OSM convention).

LOGIN.LOGIN_BUTTON: Button in an error card of the upload screen (next to 'You must be logged in') that starts the OpenStreetMap login. Short imperative verb phrase.

SEND_DATA.SEND_DATA: Screen title (header bar) of the upload screen, where pending local edits are sent to OpenStreetMap. Noun phrase or short imperative; keep it short.
SEND_DATA.DEVELOPMENT_SERVER: Banner shown at the top of the upload screen when the app is connected to OSM's test (development) server instead of the real map. 'OSM' is the project name, keep it.
SEND_DATA.YOU_MUST_BE_LOGGED_IN: Error card on the upload screen when the user is not signed in; a 'Log in' button sits right below it. Polite instruction. Keep 'OSM'.
SEND_DATA.ADDED_ITEMS: Label under a counter in the summary card (number of objects created), and screen-reader label of the change-type icon on a list row. Short noun or past participle meaning 'objects created'.
SEND_DATA.UPDATED_ITEMS: Label under a counter in the summary card (number of existing objects modified), and screen-reader label of the change-type icon of a row. Short; means 'objects updated'.
SEND_DATA.DELETED_ITEMS: Label under a counter in the summary card (number of objects deleted from the map), and screen-reader label of the change-type icon of a row. Short; means 'objects deleted'.
SEND_DATA.TOTAL_ITEMS: Short label under the total counter of the summary card, and also the heading of the list of pending changes, shown as 'Total · 5'. One word.
SEND_DATA.CHANGESET_COMMENT: Section heading and textarea placeholder for the free-text description the user gives of their edits. 'Changeset' is the established OSM term (often kept as is in translations). Max 255 characters accepted.
SEND_DATA.ERROR: Small button on a pending-change row, shown only when that change failed on upload. Tapping it opens a snackbar with the technical error text. Very short.
SEND_DATA.SEND_CHANGE: Label of the main upload button in the footer when exactly one change is pending (singular form of SEND_CHANGES). Imperative verb, short. 'Upload' means sending to OpenStreetMap.
SEND_DATA.SEND_CHANGES: Label of the main upload button in the footer when several changes are pending. {{count}} is the number of pending changes (2 or more). Imperative verb, short. Plural form of SEND_CHANGE.
SEND_DATA.DELETE: Button next to the list of pending changes that discards ALL local pending changes (after a confirmation dialog). Imperative verb, short; it deletes local edits, not OSM data.
SEND_DATA.DELETE_CONFIRM_HEADER: Title of the confirmation dialog shown before discarding all pending local changes. Short question.
SEND_DATA.DELETE_CONFIRM_MESSAGE: Body of the confirmation dialog for discarding all pending changes when there are several. {{count}} is a number of objects (2 or more). Local edits not yet uploaded are lost.
SEND_DATA.CANCEL_THIS_CHANGE: Button in the error card, shown when one specific change failed. It discards that single local change (a further confirm dialog follows). Imperative.
SEND_DATA.UPLOADING_DATA_TO_OSM: Heading of the full-screen progress overlay (with spinner) while edits are being sent. Progressive status line. Keep 'OpenStreetMap' untranslated; keep the ellipsis.
SEND_DATA.DONT_CLOSE: Sub-line under the upload progress or verification heading, asking the user to stay on the screen. Polite instruction.
SEND_DATA.RESUME_RECONCILIATION: Button in the recovery section: the server already accepted the upload, and this finishes updating the local queue to match it. Imperative. 'Reconciliation' = synchronising local data with the server's answer.
SEND_DATA.RECONCILIATION_COMPLETE: Snackbar (brief toast) confirming that a previously uncertain upload was found applied and the local data was synchronised with OpenStreetMap. Past tense.
SEND_DATA.INSPECT_CHANGESET: Link-style button opening the changeset page on openstreetmap.org in the browser. Imperative. 'Changeset' is the established OSM term.
SEND_DATA.EXPORT_RECOVERY: Button that saves a JSON file with the upload attempt and pending changes, as a backup before risky actions. Imperative. Counterpart of MARK_APPLIED, which requires it first.
SEND_DATA.MARK_NOT_APPLIED: Button in the recovery section, shown only once a check found no trace of the upload on OpenStreetMap. Opens a confirm dialog, then makes the changes editable and uploadable again. Short imperative-like label.
SEND_DATA.DISCARD_ATTEMPT_CONFIRM_HEADER: Title of the confirm dialog opened by 'Mark as not applied'. Yes/no question about the upload attempt that failed without a clear answer.
SEND_DATA.DISCARD_ATTEMPT_CONFIRM_MESSAGE: Body of the confirm dialog for marking an upload as not applied. Warns the user to verify first on OpenStreetMap; the submitted changes unlock for editing and a new upload. 'Attempt' = one upload try.
SEND_DATA.UPLOAD_LOCKED: Small status tag with a lock icon on a pending-change row that belongs to an upload whose outcome is unknown. Locked from editing until resolved. Short.
SEND_DATA.NO_PENDING_CHANGES: Empty-state text in the change list when nothing is waiting to be uploaded. Full short sentence.

ERRORS.EMPTY_QUEUE: Error message in the upload error card: the user pressed upload with nothing pending. 'Queue' is the list of local changes waiting to upload.
ERRORS.INVALID_QUEUE: Error message in the upload error card: the local list of pending changes is inconsistent (bad or contradictory entries). Technical but user-facing.
ERRORS.CONNECTION: Error message in the upload error card, also shown on the screen as a network-problem banner: the OSM server was unreachable. Keep 'OpenStreetMap'.
ERRORS.AUTHENTICATION: Error message in the upload error card: the OSM login token was rejected or expired; the user must log in again. Keep 'OpenStreetMap'.
ERRORS.CHANGESET_CLOSED: Error message in the upload error card: the changeset (OSM edit batch) was closed by the server; a retry opens a new one. Use the established translation of 'changeset'.
ERRORS.CHANGESET: Error message in the upload error card: opening the changeset failed before any data was sent. Use the established translation of 'changeset'.
ERRORS.JOURNAL: Error message in the upload error card: the local recovery journal (an on-device record of the upload in progress, used to recover after crashes) could not be written, so no upload was started.
ERRORS.UPLOAD_REJECTED: Error message in the upload error card: the server refused the data (validation error). The affected changes are listed below the message. Keep 'OpenStreetMap'.
ERRORS.UPLOAD_UNCERTAIN: Error message in the upload error card: the connection was lost during the upload, so it is unknown whether OpenStreetMap applied it. Followed by verification actions.
ERRORS.RECONCILIATION: Error message in the upload error card: the server accepted the upload, but its answer could not be matched with the local pending changes. 'Reconciled' = synchronised.
ERRORS.RECOVERY_REQUIRED: Error message in the upload error card, shown on the screen (e.g. after an app restart) when a previous upload has no known outcome. 'Inspect' = look at it on openstreetmap.org.
ERRORS.LEGACY_JOURNAL: Error message in the upload error card: a recovery journal written by an older app version cannot be processed automatically. 'Journal' = on-device upload log.
ERRORS.INTEGRITY: Error message in the upload error card: the saved copy of the data being uploaded failed a checksum validation (possibly corrupted). 'Snapshot' = saved copy.
ERRORS.LOCAL_CHANGE: Error message in the upload error card: the app could not update its on-device list of pending changes (storage problem).
ERRORS.UNKNOWN: Generic fallback error message in the upload error card when no specific cause is known. Keep 'OpenStreetMap'.
ERRORS.COMMENT_TOO_LONG: Error message in the upload error card: the changeset comment exceeds the OSM limit of 255 characters. Keep the number 255. 'Changeset' is the established OSM term.
ERRORS.FORBIDDEN: Error message in the upload error card (HTTP 403): the OSM account cannot edit. Keep 'openstreetmap.org' as is (domain name) and 'OpenStreetMap'.
ERRORS.VERSION_CONFLICT: Error message in the upload error card: edit conflict, someone else changed the same object since it was downloaded. A 'Reapply my changes' button may follow. 'Object' = OSM element; use the OSM term for conflict.
ERRORS.NODE_STILL_REFERENCED: Error message in the upload error card: the user deleted a point still used by a way or relation, so only its tags are removed. 'Line' stands for an OSM way; 'tags' is the OSM term, keep it per community usage.
ERRORS.UPLOAD_ELSEWHERE: Error message in the upload error card: another tab or window of the app is already uploading (the app was opened twice).
ERRORS.STALE_STATE: Error message in the upload error card: another tab or window of the app modified the local data. The user must reload the app (page) first.
ERRORS.RECEIPT_NOT_SAVED: Error message in the upload error card: OpenStreetMap accepted the upload but the app could not store the confirmation locally (device storage full). Important: warns NOT to upload again, to avoid duplicates.
ERRORS.LOGIN_FAILED: Snackbar message shown when tapping the 'Log in' button on the upload screen fails to open the OSM sign-in. 'Sign-in' = login process.

RECOVERY.ACTION: Row label (term in a definition list) in the upload error card; the value below is the recommended next step (one of the RECOVERY.ACTIONS strings). Short noun phrase.
RECOVERY.QUEUE: Row label in the upload error card; the value tells whether local pending changes were kept (see QUEUE_PRESERVED). 'Queue' = list of local changes awaiting upload. Short.
RECOVERY.QUEUE_PRESERVED: Value of the 'Local queue' row after a failed upload: nothing was lost. {{count}} is the number of local changes still waiting. Keep the middle dot separator. Plural-sensitive.
RECOVERY.CHANGESET: Row label in the upload error card; the value is the changeset's numeric ID (or 'Not created'). 'Changeset' is the established OSM term.
RECOVERY.STATUS: Row label in the upload error card; the value is the numeric HTTP status code returned by the OSM server (e.g. 409). Technical; 'HTTP' stays.
RECOVERY.NONE: Value of the 'Changeset' row when no changeset was created before the failure. Short, ready to follow the 'Changeset' label.

ACTIONS.EDIT_QUEUE: Value of the 'Recommended action' row: the user should edit or fix their pending changes before uploading again. Imperative, short.
ACTIONS.RECONNECT: Value of the 'Recommended action' row after a network error. Imperative, short.
ACTIONS.REAUTHENTICATE: Value of the 'Recommended action' row when login expired. Imperative, short (log in to OSM again).
ACTIONS.CREATE_CHANGESET: Value of the 'Recommended action' row when the changeset was closed. Imperative. Use the established translation of 'changeset'.
ACTIONS.INSPECT_SERVER: Value of the 'Recommended action' row when the upload outcome is unknown: look at the data on openstreetmap.org. Imperative. Keep 'OpenStreetMap'.
ACTIONS.RESUME_RECONCILIATION: Value of the 'Recommended action' row: finish synchronising local data with what the server accepted. Imperative; matches the 'Resume reconciliation' button.
ACTIONS.RETRY: Value of the 'Recommended action' row for transient failures. Imperative, short.
ACTIONS.CHECK_ACCOUNT: Value of the 'Recommended action' row after a 403 error. Imperative; two steps: log in again, then check that the OSM account is allowed to edit.
ACTIONS.RELOAD: Value of the 'Recommended action' row when another window changed the data. Imperative; matches the Reload button.

SEND_DATA.VERIFYING: Heading of the full-screen progress overlay (with spinner) while the app queries OpenStreetMap for the changeset to see if an uncertain upload was applied. Progressive status line; keep ellipsis and 'OpenStreetMap'.
SEND_DATA.VERIFY_AGAIN: Button in the recovery section that repeats the check on OpenStreetMap for an uncertain upload. Imperative, short.
SEND_DATA.VERIFICATION_NOT_FOUND: Hint line in the error card after checking the changeset on OSM: the uploaded edits are not in it. 'Changeset' is the established OSM term.
SEND_DATA.VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE: Hint line in the error card: the check on OSM failed (offline or server error). Two options: retry later via the 'Check again' button, or open the changeset via the 'Inspect changeset' button.
SEND_DATA.VERIFICATION_PARTIAL: Hint line in the error card: only some of the uploaded edits are in the changeset. Refers to the 'Export recovery data' button and the 'Consider as applied...' button. Keep UI term wording consistent.
SEND_DATA.REBASE_CHANGE: Button in the error card for an edit conflict on an object the user modified: replays the user's edits onto the latest OSM version of that object. Imperative. 'Rebase' is the key name only.
SEND_DATA.REBASE_DONE: Snackbar after the user's edits were successfully replayed on the latest server version; the user must now upload again. Past tense, then imperative.
SEND_DATA.REBASE_UP_TO_DATE: Snackbar when no conflict was found after all (object not changed on the server since download). The user can simply upload again.
SEND_DATA.REBASE_GONE: Snackbar when the object no longer exists on OpenStreetMap. 'Cancel your change' refers to the 'Cancel this change' button.
SEND_DATA.REBASE_FAILED: Snackbar when fetching the latest version of the object from OpenStreetMap failed (network). Invites a retry.
SEND_DATA.REBASE_CONFLICT: Lead-in sentence ending with a colon, followed by a bulleted list built from the three REBASE_CONFLICT_* strings (tags, position, structure). Keep the final colon.
SEND_DATA.REBASE_CONFLICT_TAGS: Bullet under 'Your changes cannot be reapplied automatically:'. Sentence fragment, lowercase start. {{keys}} is a comma-separated list of tag keys (e.g. name, opening_hours); do not translate them. 'Tags' is the OSM term.
SEND_DATA.REBASE_CONFLICT_POSITION: Bullet under 'Your changes cannot be reapplied automatically:'. Sentence fragment, lowercase start; the user moved the object and someone else moved it elsewhere on OSM.
SEND_DATA.REBASE_CONFLICT_STRUCTURE: Bullet under 'Your changes cannot be reapplied automatically:'. Sentence fragment; 'nodes' and 'members' are OSM terms (way nodes, relation members). Subject 'its' = the object.
SEND_DATA.MARK_APPLIED: Button in the recovery section; disabled until recovery data has been exported. Opens a confirm dialog, then removes the upload from the local queue because OSM already holds it. Label is long but wraps.
SEND_DATA.MARK_APPLIED_HINT: Small hint under the disabled 'Consider as applied' button: do it once recovery data export has been done. Refers to the 'Export recovery data' button.
SEND_DATA.MARK_APPLIED_CONFIRM_HEADER: Title of the confirm dialog opened by the 'Consider as applied' button. Question form.
SEND_DATA.MARK_APPLIED_CONFIRM_MESSAGE: Body of that confirm dialog. Warns to continue only if the OSM server holds the edits; they leave the local queue, a copy remains in the exported file; the user should re-download the map area to see the updated objects.
SEND_DATA.ATTEMPT_ABANDONED: Snackbar after confirming 'Consider as applied': the upload attempt is no longer in the local queue. Past tense passive.
SEND_DATA.STALE_WINDOW: Warning card at the top of the upload screen when another tab or window of the app changed the local data; a 'Reload' button is below it. 'Window' means browser tab or app window.
SEND_DATA.RELOAD: Button label that reloads the app (page reload); appears in the stale-data warning card and in the recovery actions. Imperative, short.
SEND_DATA.QUARANTINE_MESSAGE: Warning card text: some saved local objects were corrupted and moved aside instead of being lost. {{count}} is a number of objects. Followed by Export and Dismiss buttons. Plural-sensitive.
SEND_DATA.QUARANTINE_EXPORT: Button label that saves a JSON file of unreadable local objects (or of local data backups, a second card). Imperative, short; used in two warning cards.
SEND_DATA.QUARANTINE_DISMISS: Button in the warning card that deletes the set-aside unreadable objects from the device after a confirm dialog. Imperative, short (dismiss/ignore).
SEND_DATA.QUARANTINE_DISMISS_CONFIRM_HEADER: Title of the confirm dialog for deleting the set-aside unreadable objects. Question form.
SEND_DATA.QUARANTINE_DISMISS_CONFIRM_MESSAGE: Body of that confirm dialog. Permanent deletion on this device; warns to proceed only after export. 'Unreadable objects' = corrupted local OSM objects.
SEND_DATA.EXPORT_FAILED: Snackbar error shown when saving or sharing an exported JSON file (recovery data, unreadable objects, backups) fails.
SEND_DATA.DELETE_CONFIRM_MESSAGE_ONE: Body of the confirmation dialog for discarding pending changes when there is exactly one (singular of DELETE_CONFIRM_MESSAGE; no placeholder). Local edit lost permanently.
SEND_DATA.VERIFICATION_WAIT: Hint line in the error card: a check found nothing but OSM may still process a delayed request. {{seconds}} is a whole number of seconds counting down. Keep 's' (seconds) abbreviation style per language.
SEND_DATA.VERIFICATION_CHECK_NOW: Hint line in the error card shown when the countdown ended; tells the user to press 'Check again' to confirm the upload was not applied.
SEND_DATA.STATE_BACKUP_MESSAGE: Warning card text on the upload screen (with an Export button): the app set local data aside when the user reset it or switched OSM server. Export lets them keep any unsent edits it contained.

SETTINGS.SETTINGS: Title of the Settings screen header (top bar). Short noun. Same word as the menu item MENU.SETTINGS.
SETTINGS.MAP: Section heading in Settings grouping the map display toggles (position, orientation, polygons, lines, icons). Short noun, shown with a map icon.
SETTINGS.POSITION_TRACKING: Toggle label in Settings > Map (also its screen-reader label). When on, the map keeps following the user's GPS location. Short.
SETTINGS.POSITION_TRACKING_HINT: Description under the 'Position tracking' toggle. Describes what happens while the setting is on. Full sentence.
SETTINGS.ORIENTATION_TRACKING: Toggle label in Settings > Map (also its screen-reader label). When on, the map rotates according to the phone's compass/heading. Short.
SETTINGS.ORIENTATION_TRACKING_HINT: Description under the 'Orientation tracking' toggle. 'Device' means the phone or tablet's compass sensor. Full sentence.
SETTINGS.HIDE_LARGE_POLYGON: Toggle label in Settings > Map (also its screen-reader label). Polygons are map areas (buildings, parks...). '5000 m²' is a fixed value written in the text: keep the number and unit (adapt number formatting only if needed).
SETTINGS.HIDE_LARGE_POLYGON_HINT: Description under the 'Hide polygons larger than 5000 m²' toggle. Marker = the pin shown on the map for an object. Keep the fixed value 5000 m² consistent with the label.
SETTINGS.HIDE_LONG_LINE: Toggle label in Settings > Map (also its screen-reader label). Lines are linear map features (roads, paths, fences...). '200 m' is a fixed value: keep it consistent with the hint.
SETTINGS.HIDE_LONG_LINE_HINT: Description under the 'Hide lines longer than 200 m' toggle. Marker = the pin shown on the map for the line. Keep 200 m consistent with the label.
SETTINGS.TAGS: Section heading in Settings grouping survey-date and tag-related options. 'Tags' is the OpenStreetMap term (key=value pairs on an object); use the established OSM translation. Short noun, shown with a tag icon.
SETTINGS.DATA: Section heading in Settings for data-loading options (memory limit, download margin). Short noun.
SETTINGS.MARGIN: Label of a slider in Settings > Data; the current value in metres (e.g. '50 m') is appended right after this text. Short noun, no trailing colon.
SETTINGS.MARGIN_HINT: Description under the 'Margin' slider. The margin is extra distance, in metres, around the visible map area for which OpenStreetMap data is downloaded.
SETTINGS.AERIAL_IMAGERY: Title of the Aerial imagery screen and label of a main-menu item (short, fits one menu row). Satellite/orthophoto background maps the user picks to trace over. Noun phrase.
SETTINGS.AERIAL_IMAGERY_HINT: Intro line at the top of the Aerial imagery screen, directly above a grid of selectable imagery cards. Ends with a colon because a list follows.
SETTINGS.LANGUAGE_AND_REGION: Section heading in Settings grouping the language and country selectors. Short noun phrase.
SETTINGS.UI_LANGUAGE: Label of a dropdown in Settings: language of the app's own interface (menus, buttons, messages). Not the language of OSM tags.
SETTINGS.TAG_LANGUAGE: Label of a dropdown in Settings: language used for tag/preset names and descriptions (e.g. type of place) shown in the object editor. Distinct from the interface language.
SETTINGS.TAG_COUNTRY: Label of a dropdown in Settings: country used to pick country-specific tag presets. Single word/noun.
SETTINGS.TAG_COUNTRY_HINT: Description under the 'Country' dropdown. 'Tags' is the OSM term; 'presets' are predefined object types/templates in the editor.
SETTINGS.CACHE: Section heading in Settings for clearing locally stored data. Short noun phrase.
SETTINGS.DELETE_CACHE: Label of a row in Settings > Cache whose button deletes all locally stored app data. Describes the action (verb phrase).
SETTINGS.DELETE_CACHE_HINT: Description under 'Delete entire app cache'. 'Edits' = local changes not yet uploaded to OpenStreetMap; 'login' = the OSM sign-in session.
SETTINGS.DISPLAY_OLD_TAGS_ICON: Toggle label in Settings > Map (also its screen-reader label). Old objects are OSM objects whose last modification is old, i.e. possibly outdated data.
SETTINGS.OLD_TAGS_ICON_RANGE_PART_1: First half of one sentence shown above a slider; a bold number of years (e.g. '2') is inserted after it, then OLD_TAGS_ICON_RANGE_PART_2 follows. Must read naturally with a number in between; no trailing punctuation.
SETTINGS.OLD_TAGS_ICON_RANGE_PART_2: Second half of a sentence: it follows the bold number of years inserted after OLD_TAGS_ICON_RANGE_PART_1 (e.g. '2 years ago'). Keep the word order compatible with the number coming first.
SETTINGS.OLD_TAGS_ICON_HINT: Description under the 'Show an icon on old objects' toggle. The icon is a small badge next to the object's marker on the map. 'Object' = OSM feature.
SETTINGS.DISPLAY_FIXME_ICON: Toggle label in Settings > Map (also its screen-reader label). 'fixme' is the OSM tag key (fixme=...) meaning the object needs review: keep the word fixme in quotes as the tag name.
SETTINGS.DISPLAY_FIXME_ICON_HINT: Description under the 'Display fixme icons' toggle. Keep 'fixme' as is: it is the OSM tag name, shown in the sentence as a tag.
SETTINGS.ADD_SURVEY_DATE: Toggle label in Settings > Tags (also its screen-reader label). When on, a survey date tag is written automatically on each add/edit. 'Survey' = on-the-ground verification, OSM term.
SETTINGS.ADD_SURVEY_DATE_HINT: Description under the 'Add the survey date' toggle. 'Survey date tag' refers to the tag chosen in the dropdown below (survey:date or check_date); 'today's date' is the current date.
SETTINGS.CHECKED_KEY: Label of a dropdown in Settings > Tags to choose which tag key records the survey date. Options are the literal tag keys survey:date and check_date, never translated.
SETTINGS.LINES_SELECTABLE: Toggle label in Settings > Map (also its screen-reader label). Lines are linear map features (roads, paths...). Imperative-style phrase.
SETTINGS.LINES_SELECTABLE_HINT: Description under the 'Make lines selectable' toggle. 'Element sheet' is the bottom panel showing the details/editor of the selected object (same as 'object sheet' elsewhere).
SETTINGS.POLYGONS_SELECTABLE: Toggle label in Settings > Map (also its screen-reader label). Polygons are map areas (buildings, parks...). Imperative-style phrase.
SETTINGS.POLYGONS_SELECTABLE_HINT: Description under the 'Make polygons selectable' toggle. 'Element sheet' is the panel showing the details/editor of the selected object.
SETTINGS.SWITCH_SERVER_CONFIRM: Confirm button of a destructive confirmation dialog (switching between the OSM production server and the OSM development server). Verb phrase, short, imperative.
SETTINGS.SWITCH_SERVER_MESSAGE: Body of the confirmation dialog shown when toggling the OSM development server while there are local edits not yet uploaded. 'Pending local edit' = change made on the phone, not yet sent to OpenStreetMap. Followed by a possible extra paragraph.
SETTINGS.SWITCH_SERVER_TITLE: Title of the confirmation dialog shown when toggling 'Use the OSM development server'. A question. 'Server' = the OpenStreetMap API server (production vs. development/test). Keep 'OpenStreetMap' as is.
SETTINGS.CENTER_WHEN_GPS_IS_READY: Toggle label in Settings > Map (also its screen-reader label). At app startup, the map automatically recentres on the user's GPS position once available.
SETTINGS.CENTER_WHEN_GPS_IS_READY_HINT: Description under the 'On start, center the map on your location' toggle. 'As soon as possible' = as soon as a GPS fix is obtained.
SETTINGS.OPEN_OBJECT_SHEET_AS_PREVIEW: Toggle label in Settings > Map (also its screen-reader label). 'Object sheet' = the panel with the details of a tapped OSM object; 'preview' = a half-height partial view.
SETTINGS.OPEN_OBJECT_SHEET_AS_PREVIEW_HINT: Description under the 'Open objects as a preview' toggle. 'Object sheet' is the details panel; 'halfway' = half the screen height; 'Otherwise' = when the toggle is off.
SETTINGS.LIMIT_FEATURES: Label of a slider in Settings > Data; the current number (e.g. '10000') is appended right after the text. 'Objects' = OSM features held in the phone's memory. No trailing colon.
SETTINGS.LIMIT_FEATURES_HINT: Description under the 'Maximum number of objects in memory' slider. 'Old data' = previously downloaded objects far from the view; 'current modifications' = the user's unsent edits. Warns about performance. Text has no final period in English.
SETTINGS.DISPLAY_SURVEY_CARD: Label of a dropdown in Settings > Tags. The 'survey card' is a small card in the object sheet/editor to mark an object as surveyed today. 'Survey' is an OSM term.
SETTINGS.DISPLAY_SURVEY_CARD_HINT: Description under the 'Show the survey card' dropdown. 'Survey date' = value of survey:date / check_date tag recorded for an object.

DISPLAY_SURVEY_CARD_CHOICE.NEVER: Option of the 'Show the survey card' dropdown. Single word meaning the card is never shown.
DISPLAY_SURVEY_CARD_CHOICE.OLDER: Option of the 'Show the survey card' dropdown: show the card only for objects whose last update is older than a threshold set by a slider appearing below. Ends with '...' because a duration follows.
DISPLAY_SURVEY_CARD_CHOICE.ALWAYS: Option of the 'Show the survey card' dropdown. Single word meaning the card is always shown.

SETTINGS.SURVEY_CARD_RANGE: Label above a slider (shown when the survey card option is 'Older than...'). {{year}} is a number of years, possibly with a half (e.g. 0.5, 2, 3.5): handle pluralisation for non-integers.
SETTINGS.UPLOAD_IN_PROGRESS: Snackbar (toast) and inline warning in Settings > Cache, shown when the user tries to delete the cache or switch server while an upload to OpenStreetMap is running. Two short sentences.
SETTINGS.DELETE_CACHE_CONFIRM_TITLE: Title of the confirmation dialog before deleting all app data. A question.
SETTINGS.DELETE_CACHE_CONFIRM_MESSAGE: First paragraph of the 'Delete the entire cache?' dialog; further warning paragraphs may follow. 'Remembered fields' = values the app saved to prefill forms. 'Login' = OSM sign-in session. Irreversible.
SETTINGS.DELETE_CACHE_PENDING_ONE: Extra warning paragraph in the delete-cache dialog when exactly one local edit is waiting to be uploaded. Singular form; 'OpenStreetMap' stays as is.
SETTINGS.DELETE_CACHE_PENDING_MANY: Extra warning paragraph in the delete-cache dialog when several local edits are waiting. {{count}} is an integer >= 2. Plural form; 'OpenStreetMap' stays as is.
SETTINGS.DELETE_CACHE_UNRESOLVED_UPLOAD: Extra warning paragraph in the delete-cache dialog when an earlier upload ended in an uncertain state (unknown whether it reached OpenStreetMap). 'Recovery record' = local journal used to check the upload later; 'duplicates' = objects created twice on OSM.
SETTINGS.DELETE_CACHE_CONFIRM: Confirm button of the delete-cache dialog (destructive, red). Imperative verb phrase, short; the cancel button sits next to it.
SETTINGS.DEVELOPER_MODE: Section heading at the bottom of Settings (bug icon) for developer options. Short noun phrase.
SETTINGS.DEV_SERVER: Toggle label in Settings > Developer mode: use the OSM development (sandbox/test) server instead of the real OpenStreetMap one, so edits don't touch real data. Keep 'OSM' as is.
SETTINGS.DEV_SERVER_HINT: Description under the 'Use the OSM development server' toggle. 'Data' = downloaded map data; app restarts after confirmation.
SETTINGS.SWITCH_SERVER_MESSAGE_CLEAN: Body of the confirmation dialog when toggling the OSM development server and there are no pending edits. 'Signs you out' = ends the OSM login session; 'downloaded data' = cached map data.
SETTINGS.AERIAL_IMAGERY_ERROR: Error message in the Aerial imagery screen when the imagery list fails to load; a 'Retry' button appears below it. Full sentences.
SETTINGS.SWITCH_SERVER_UNRESOLVED_UPLOAD: Extra warning paragraph in the server-switch dialog when an earlier upload is in an uncertain state. 'Recovery record' = local journal used to verify the upload; 'duplicates' = objects created twice on OSM.
SETTINGS.SWITCH_SERVER_FAILED: Snackbar (toast) shown when switching OSM server fails because the local data backup could not be made; the server stays unchanged. Full sentence, reassuring.

MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.CUSTOM_KEY_VALUE: Label of a button that expands, and heading of the section it opens, in the category picker, letting the user type their own OSM tag key and value. Also the label of a text field in a multi-select. Keep short; 'value' here is the OSM tag value.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.CUSTOM_TAG_INVALID: Inline error under the custom tag form when the typed OSM tag key or value is empty or has invalid characters. '1 to 255' is the OSM length limit; 'tag', 'key' and 'value' are OSM terms.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.CUSTOM_TAG_COLLISION: Inline error under the custom tag form: the typed key=value pair is already covered by one of the app's predefined categories (presets), so it cannot be added as a custom tag. 'Category' is the app's name for a preset.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.SEARCH_TAG_AT_LEAST_3_LETTERS: Hint shown in place of search results in the category/tag search (picker and tag management dialog) until the query is long enough. Despite the key name, it counts characters of any script.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.LOADING: Short status text under a spinner while the object editor is loading or saving. Ends with an ellipsis character.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.META_MYSELF: Stands for the author name in the object sheet history line (e.g. 'Updated 3 days ago · Myself') when the last edit is the user's own, not yet uploaded to OpenStreetMap. Appears in bold as a person's name.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.NO_NAME: Fallback title for a map object that has no name tag. Shown in the object sheet header, in the list of overlapping objects, and in the upload list. Short.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.PLACEHOLDER_NAME: Placeholder and screen-reader label of the text field for the object's name (the OSM 'name' tag) at the top of the editor. A single word, noun.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.SAVE_CHANGE: Label of the primary save button of the object editor when exactly one field has been modified. Imperative verb; the number 1 is fixed. Saving stores the edit locally, it does not upload yet.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.SAVE_CHANGES: Label of the primary save button of the object editor when several fields were modified. {{count}} is an integer greater than 1. Imperative verb; saves locally, no upload yet. Plural form needed.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.ADD_A_TAG: Title of the dialog, opened from the object editor, in which the user picks an extra field or OSM tag to add to the object. 'Tag' is the established OSM term.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.DELETE_CONFIRM_HEADER: Title of the confirmation dialog shown before the user cancels or deletes their pending edit of an object. Short generic question, with a destructive confirm button.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.DELETE_CONFIRM_MESSAGE: Body of the confirmation dialog asking whether to delete the selected map object (a point, from the editor or object sheet). 'Item' means the map object, not a list entry.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.SELECT_CATEGORY: Title of the full-screen dialog where the user picks the category (preset, e.g. restaurant, bench) of a new or existing object. Imperative; also used as accessible title.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.THIS_NODE_IS_USED_BY_A_WAY: Warning notice in the object sheet: the point is a vertex of one or more lines/areas, which matters for deletion. {{count}} is the number of ways (1 or more). 'way(s)' is the OSM term 'way'; 'node' means point.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.UNDEFINED_VALUE: Text for a field with no value set, shown as a grey placeholder in a preset field and as the empty first option of a dropdown. Means value not specified; keep it short, an abbreviation is acceptable.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.LAST_TAG_USED: Label of one of two toggle buttons (with an icon) in the category picker, showing the categories the user used most recently. Pairs with the Bookmarks toggle. Short.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.BOOKMARKS: Label of one of two toggle buttons (with a heart icon) in the category picker, listing the categories the user saved as favorites. Pairs with the Last used tags toggle. Short.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.ADD_TAG_PLACEHOLDER: Placeholder of the search field in the Add a tag dialog; the user types an OSM tag key (e.g. opening_hours) or a field name to filter the list. 'Key' is the OSM term.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.SURVEY_QUESTION: Question on the survey card of the object sheet, asking a person standing at the location to confirm that the object still exists. Answered with Yes/No buttons; answering Yes refreshes its check date.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.WARN_NODE_EDITED: Notice in the object sheet and editor footer telling the user this object has been edited on the device and not yet uploaded to OpenStreetMap. Followed by a button to cancel the edit.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.VALUE_LIMIT: Hint under a text field when it reaches the OSM maximum length. {{max}} is the number 255. Plural form of 'characters' may be needed.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.VALUE_TOO_LONG: Toast shown when saving is blocked because a tag value exceeds the OSM length limit. {{key}} is an OSM tag key (e.g. name, opening_hours), keep it untranslated; {{max}} is 255. Quotes around the key are typographic.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.VALUE_INVALID: Toast shown when saving is blocked because a tag value contains characters (e.g. control characters) rejected by the OpenStreetMap API; also an inline error under a field. {{key}} is an OSM tag key, keep it as is.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.FIELDS_REMEMBERED: Toast confirming that the user's current field values were saved to be reused for the next new object of that category. {{category}} is the category (preset) name, e.g. Restaurant, already translated.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.UPLOAD_LOCKED: Toast shown when saving fails because the object is part of an upload to OpenStreetMap that is still pending or uncertain. 'Upload' means sending changes to OSM; the user must finish that from the upload screen.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.CUSTOM_VALUE_HINT: Hint under the custom tag heading in the category picker, warning the user not to invent values: use only for a real OSM value missing from the app's list. Mentions OpenStreetMap by name; keep it untranslated.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.SURVEY_NO_NODE_ONLY: Hint under the survey card Yes/No buttons, shown when the object is not a point (it is a line or area), explaining why No is disabled. Quoted No must match the translation of the No button; 'point' means OSM node.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.SHOW_ALL_OPTIONS: Toggle button label under a long checkbox list in the editor; expands the list. {{count}} is the total number of options (an integer, usually above 6). Plural form may be needed.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.SHOW_FEWER_OPTIONS: Toggle button label that collapses the expanded long option list in the editor back to its first items. Pairs with Show all {{count}} options.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.REMOVE_VALUE: Screen-reader label (aria-label) of the small X button on a value chip in a multi-value field (e.g. cuisine). {{value}} is the displayed value, e.g. Pizza. Imperative verb; not visible text.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.ADD_VALUE: Floating label of the text field to type one more value in a multi-value field (OSM values separated by semicolons, e.g. cuisine). Short, imperative or noun phrase.
MODAL_SELECTED_ITEM.ADD_VALUE_TO: Screen-reader label (aria-label, not visible) of the same add-value text field. {{field}} is the field's translated label (e.g. Cuisine), or the raw OSM key if none. Keep placeholder as is.

ALERT.TAG_IS_DEPRECATED: Error notice at the top of the object editor when an object uses a deprecated OSM tag (one the community has replaced by another). 'Tag' and 'deprecated' follow OSM terminology. Short sentence, no period.
ALERT.FIX: Button next to the 'This tag is deprecated' notice that automatically replaces the old tag with the recommended one. Short imperative verb (wrench icon).

MANAGE_TAGS.TAG_MANAGEMENT_TITLE: Title of the settings screen listing three cards (active, hidden, favorite tags). 'Tags' here means the app's categories of map objects (presets), not raw OSM tags. Screen header, short.
MANAGE_TAGS.ACTIVE_TAGS: Heading of a card on the tag management screen, also the title of the dialog it opens and part of the aria-label of its Open button. Imperative, matching the two sibling headings (hidden, favorites).
MANAGE_TAGS.ACTIVE_TAGS_DESCRIPTION: Description under the active tags heading. 'Items' are categories of map objects. 'Hide' means stop displaying them on the map; 'favourites' are bookmarked categories. The window is the dialog opened by the Open button.
MANAGE_TAGS.HIDDEN_TAGS_WARNING: Warning in the active tags card, shown in a highlight style. Explains the consequence of hiding a category: not drawn on the map nor offered when adding objects, so users may create duplicate objects.
MANAGE_TAGS.HIDDEN_TAGS: Heading of a card on the tag management screen, also dialog title and part of an Open button aria-label. Imperative, same pattern as 'Manage active tags'.
MANAGE_TAGS.HIDDEN_TAGS_DESCRIPTION: Description under the hidden tags heading, also the empty-state message of the hidden tags dialog. Hidden items are categories the user chose to hide; 'visible' means shown again on the map.
MANAGE_TAGS.BOOKMARKED_TAGS: Heading of a card on the tag management screen, also dialog title and part of an Open button aria-label. 'Favorites' are the categories saved with a heart icon. Imperative.
MANAGE_TAGS.BOOKMARKED_TAGS_DESCRIPTION: Description under the favorites heading, also text in the favorites dialog. 'Favorite tags' are bookmarked categories shown in the category picker.
MANAGE_TAGS.RESET_HIDDEN_TAGS: Footer button of the hidden tags dialog: restores the default set of hidden categories. Imperative, one word if possible; sits next to 'Remove all' and Close.
MANAGE_TAGS.REMOVE_ALL_HIDDEN_TAGS: Footer button (styled as dangerous) of the hidden tags dialog: un-hides every category at once, making them all visible again. Not a deletion of data. Imperative, short.
MANAGE_TAGS.OPEN: Label of a button with a right chevron on each card of the tag management screen; opens that card's dialog. Imperative verb; also read aloud before the card title (e.g. Open · Manage your favorites).

DAYS.MONDAY: Full weekday name, capitalized as the language requires. Used in a list of schedule rows (row header) and as the screen-reader label of the day toggle buttons in the opening hours editor. Monday is the first day.
DAYS.TUESDAY: Full weekday name (not an abbreviation). Row header in the opening hours table and screen-reader label of a day toggle button. Visible short day buttons are generated by the app, not from this text.
DAYS.WEDNESDAY: Full weekday name (not an abbreviation). Row header in the opening hours table and screen-reader label of a day toggle button. Length is not constrained.
DAYS.THURSDAY: Full weekday name (not an abbreviation). Row header in the opening hours table and screen-reader label of a day toggle button. Length is not constrained.
DAYS.FRIDAY: Full weekday name (not an abbreviation). Row header in the opening hours table and screen-reader label of a day toggle button. Length is not constrained.
DAYS.SATURDAY: Full weekday name (not an abbreviation). Row header in the opening hours table and screen-reader label of a day toggle button. Length is not constrained.
DAYS.SUNDAY: Full weekday name (not an abbreviation). Row header in the opening hours table and screen-reader label of a day toggle button. Sunday is the last day in this app's week.

OPENINGHOURS.CLOSED: Shown in the opening hours table in the cell of a weekday that has no opening interval. Adjective, one word.
OPENINGHOURS.UNKNOW: Shown when an object has no opening_hours value, in the opening hours field. Means the hours are not specified or not known; keep neutral, not 'closed'. (Key name has a typo, ignore.)
OPENINGHOURS.START_TIME: Floating label of a time input (opening time) in the opening hours interval dialog. Pairs with End Time. Short; in French-like languages 'From' phrasing is fine.
OPENINGHOURS.END_TIME: Floating label of a time input (closing time) in the interval dialog. Also reused in a screen-reader label with ' 24:00' appended, so it must work as the start of such a phrase. Pairs with Start Time.
OPENINGHOURS.ADD_OPENING_HOURS: Label of a button with a plus icon in the object editor's opening hours field, shown when no hours are set. Opens the interval dialog. Imperative.
OPENINGHOURS.EDIT_OPENING_HOURS: Label of a button with a calendar-edit icon in the object editor's opening hours field, shown when hours already exist. Opens the interval dialog. Imperative.
OPENINGHOURS.MANAGE_OPENING_HOURS: Title of the opening hours dialog (clock icon) where the user sets days and time ranges. Imperative, matches the Add/Edit buttons.
OPENINGHOURS.ADD_INTERVAL: Button (plus icon) in a schedule group of the dialog: adds another time range (e.g. a lunch break split) to the same days. 'Interval' = time range, matches 'Delete this interval'. Imperative.
OPENINGHOURS.ADD_SCHEDULE_GROUP: Button in the opening hours dialog adding a new group of days with their own time ranges, e.g. different hours on Saturday. Imperative; 'other days' means days not yet configured.
OPENINGHOURS.SCHEDULE_GROUP: Heading of each group of days in the opening hours dialog. {{ number }} is the group's position, an integer starting at 1 (keep the spaces inside braces as is). A noun like 'Schedule 1', 'Hours 1'.
OPENINGHOURS.DELETE_SCHEDULE_GROUP: Screen-reader label (aria-label) of the trash icon button removing a group of days in the dialog; only shown with 2+ groups. Imperative; not visible text.
OPENINGHOURS.SAVE_OPENING_HOURS: Label of the primary button at the bottom of the opening hours dialog; validates and writes the opening_hours value into the object (edit stays local). Imperative.
OPENINGHOURS.DELETE_INTERVAL: Screen-reader label (aria-label) of a trash/close icon button deleting one time range, in the dialog and in the field's table. Not visible text. Imperative.
OPENINGHOURS.SELECT_AT_LEAST_ONE_DAY: Inline warning in a schedule group when none of the weekday toggle buttons is selected, blocking save. Addresses the user.
OPENINGHOURS.TOO_COMPLEX_FOR_OSMGO: Note shown under the raw opening_hours code when its syntax (e.g. holidays, seasons, week numbers) cannot be edited with the visual editor. 'Osm Go!' is the app name, keep it unchanged.
OPENINGHOURS.NEXT_DAY: Small hint under a time range whose end time is earlier than its start (e.g. 22:00 to 02:00), meaning closing happens after midnight, on the following day.

ERRORS.INVALID_TIME: Inline error (alert) under a time range when the start or end time is empty or malformed. Addresses the user, imperative.
ERRORS.SAME_TIME: Inline error (alert) under a time range whose start and end times are identical, which is not a valid interval.
ERRORS.OVERLAP: Inline error (alert) under a time range that overlaps another time range of the same days. 'Range' is the same notion as 'interval' elsewhere.
ERRORS.NO_RANGE: Inline warning in a schedule group that has no time range yet; it blocks saving. Imperative.
